items.body: "There is no such thing as a stranger�s children." - old Ukrainian saying I�ve long been affected, indeed somewhat obsessed, by what�s happening in Ukraine, partly because of one of my favorite bands, DakhaBrakha. I went to Kyiv to see them at the time of the Maidan protests, just after the shooting by snipers of over a hundred protesters. I intentionally didn�t read this album�s booklet notes before listening, so that I could react to it without sympathetic pre-judgement, just as music. It�s strong musically and vocally by any standards, Ukrainian or otherwise. When I did then turn to the notes that translate and explain the songs, I had that rare experience, for me, of becoming moist-eyed. The songs are a mix of traditional and original. They are focused on the abduction by Russia of about 20,000 Ukrainian children who have been taken from their parents in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine and sent to Russia, in an attempt to turn them into haters of their native land and people. It�s a heinous war crime. Marichka is a Ukrainian-Canadian singer who moves between Canada and her homeland. For this album she�s gathered two groups of musicians, one in each country. Both ensembles contribute vocals and instrumentation, mostly bowed strings, plus some bandura and piano. The group in Ukraine includes Lisa from the destroyed and invaded city of Mariupol, playing a solo on double ocarina; at 16 she was one of the stolen children but managed to return to Ukraine. Daughters of Donbas � co-led by Marichka and singer/bandurist Alina Kuzma, who shares the lead vocal role � is an all-female ensemble in Canada that tours performing these songs. �Foreign Land� is a reworking of a traditional song about the young girls who were sent away to work in foreign households - Marichka�s grandmother was one of these - that can also be taken to refer to the plight of today�s stolen children. The translation goes: A mother packed up her daughter To leave for a strange land To a strange land with strange people Oh, who will pity you, my daughter? Those who will beat me will pity me I'll never again live with you, my mother When, my daughter, should I expect you to come home? When the grass in the garden grows, my mother The grass grew and grew and began to dry The mother was waiting for her daughter to return, and began to cry Did you hear, my mother, how I came to you? How I flew as a bird above your window? How I cooed like a dove? If, my daughter, I could hear you I would open all the doors and windows To let you fly in Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Alina Kuzma, Zo� Santo As befits the song, Marichka�s vocal here is gentle. But in the second track, �Rusalka,� with Alina Kuzma taking the lead vocals, things turn harsh and fierce. A rusalka is a mythical creature, a nature spirit of fields, forest and rivers, that features in traditional ritual songs. The melody of this one is by Zo� Santo and Kuzma, with lyrics drawing on tradition and the composition of Santo and 19thC Ukrainian poet and folklorist Taras Shevchenko. An ominous double-bass drone, chunking strings, a slithering vocal that moves into sections of white-voice fast recitative and expands into a soaring wild cry. The lyrics are very dark, perhaps evoking the hell of the front line: Home a hell of old growth stumps Marsh a mud of memories Don�t get bogged down in these parts Your kind won�t last a day in here While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. A rusalka sat on a white birch, rusalky asked girls for shirts. Long fingers and nails so sharp Tongue forked round serrated teeth Moss grows down beneath her parts Weeds braided from ear to ear While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. �Girls, my friends, give me your shirts. Though I�m thin, give me a thin one.� Here live us the backless ones Many voices of dead sons You are right to quake in fear Send your sinful children here �Who Am I� is a plea of separation and disorientation, the pain and confusion of an abducted child, contrasting �the human in me� and �the creature in me,� like an internalized riddle-song, with the refrain, in English: Who am I for you? Who am I for me? Do you know me? Really know me? �Enchantress,� passionately sung by Kuzma to her own bandura accompaniment, a girl�s lament of the loss of her brave love taken from her by the enchantress, who is an allegory of war, is based on a traditional song and uses that style of melody and lyrics, �Riddle,� sung by Marichka, reworks a traditional riddle song to be the riddles told by the grandfather of a child, 12-year-old Kira from Mariupol, who experienced the death of her father and her abduction to Russia. Her grandfather tracked her down, and brought her back, traumatized, and asked her riddles - as the notes say �to jog her memory, and remind her who she was, where her home was, and of her family�s love for her.� Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �4.5.0� is a military expression for �all�s well� or �all is quiet.� The song is a message, as from a mother, to a stolen child. Marichka�s voice is cherishing: Remember this: I am with you, I am here Don't give up, I'm with you. Don't give up, I'm with you Your hope is my weapon Don't be sad, I'm with you 4.5.0. will be again �breaking into a tearing howl: And when the world's axis breaks When the sky folds like a parchment Out of nowhere her words will come� �and back to fragile reassurance �It's all right, I'm here, I'm here� "Lullaby," based on a traditional lullaby, sung by Alina Kuzma to accompaniment by her bandura and Zo� Santo's viola, starts in gentle lullaby style, but moves to a lament; it's for the stolen children and those who, as the notes put it, 'have been stolen for ever.' Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �Remember, I Believe in You� is a powerful piece of harmonizing vocals and slithering strings. Here�s the story it�s based on: Yevhen lived in Mariupol with his three young children. During the siege they lived in a basement bomb shelter for months. One day, Russian soldiers entered their bomb shelter. Yevhen was taken to a filtration camp and separated from his children who were all taken to a hospital and then to Russian summer �camp�. In the filtration camp Yevhen was brutally tortured and forced to sleep standing on one leg. He tried to fall asleep, whispering prayers for his children: �Everything will be fine, I believe in you.� After his release he walked 30 kilometers to the place where his children had been taken but it was too late. They had already been sent to Moscow. Yevhen learned of this after receiving a text from one of his children who had found an unattended device. He traveled thousands of kilometers, crossed the borders of three countries, endured checks, interrogations and danger to reach Moscow and take his children home. All those days he tirelessly repeated to himself, �I believe in myself, I believe in my kids. Everything will be good.� �Another Heaven,� sung by Marichka with the ensemble in Ukraine, is inspired by another heart-rending story: Ilya was 9 years old when his mother was killed by a rocket strike right in front of him. He was taken to a hospital in occupied Donetsk, where 15 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body without anesthesia. After he appeared in a report on Russian television, Ilya�s grandmother learned his location. She managed to bring her grandson to Kyiv, where he lives now, experiencing missile attacks every night. At age 11, he says that it is up to everyone to fight enemies, to protect other cities, and to build another heaven, where your home will not be destroyed. In 2014, during the Kyiv Maidan protests, Marichka wrote and performed �Red Boots Tango,� using a melody she�d put to a poem by Taras Shevchenko. For this album she sings it again in Ukraine, with the ensemble there adding swirling, classic tango-style strings. Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, BanduraGirl The final track on the album is a solo, recorded in Kyiv, by Anastasiya Voytyuk, accompanying herself on the older, simpler form of bandura that was used by kobzars to accompany epic poetry, and also on the nowadays more well-known big, heavy form developed from it in Soviet times that was made mainly in the piano factory at Chernihiv. Her song, �Soon I Will Be Back,� is based on a poem by novelist, journalist and war crime researcher Victoria Amelia, who was killed in 2023, in the city of Kramatorsk in Donbas, by a Russian rocket. Find the artist online. Further reading: Otava Yo - Do You Love (Review) Sofia Rei - Umbral (Review)

items.body: For an overview of the what, the why, and the where of this music, do read my review of Volume 1 of this series. Essentially, this collection is more of what made Volume 1 so infectious. Yet, what makes this music so fascinating in general, that is, beyond its unswerving ability to fill dance floors, is the fact that these two islands, part of the Paises Africanos de Lingua Oficial Portuguesa (PALOP) regions of the world, are the second smallest African country; Seychelles is smaller. There are only 12 villages on Sao Tom�, lots of rain forest and, not surprisingly, lots of rain. I mention this because one could be fooled into thinking, with music like what�s on offer here, there must have been a music scene larger than there actually was. Not that little was happening, but that less got recorded or released than it might have had there been a city such as Lagos or Nairobi with the studios, labels, and pressing plants to better document it all. The music here, like Volume 1- recorded during Africa�s so-called golden age- is known as Puxa, a complex stew of ingredients from other former African Portuguese colonies mixed with rhythms that, with the help of dancers, can summon spirits or exorcise demons. At least according to some. It�s worth knowing that a 100 years or so ago, the Portuguese banned Puxa dance; it�s also worth knowing they appear to have failed miserably at this silly endeavor. Tucked away in modern Puxa is merengue, Kompas, Soukouss, Benga, and much else. One suspects much of this is coincidental, while other grooves were definitely imported considering both Portuguese rule and the islands� location over the Atlantic from the Caribbean. But don�t be fooled into thinking these two islands don�t have their own thing, as the sounds on this collection show. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s - Pedro Lima Pedro Lima, who has featured in his own Bongo Joe collection, leads a fiery band, complete with choked guitar vamps tussling with a kit drummer as a lead guitar comments from the sidelines on �Sossegado.� Elsewhere, Sangazuza demonstrates what happens when the bass and keys drop out, leaving the drummers and guitars to ride out a groove and drive dancers mad in the process. Check �Sono s� ku� de t�ma� or �Mairo bi cedo� for their ability to place a firm finger on the pulse. Over 15 tracks, the collection shows off multiple guitars weaving and circling one another, with lead and harmony vocals constantly in response, becoming part of the songs� melodic framework. At any given moment, vocals give way as the music unspools and floats on grooves that must have gone on for hours live. Africa Negra�s �Apoi�mos a luta dos nossos irm�os� is one example. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s by Various Artists In general, what�s on offer here, like Volume 1, was recorded at Radio Sao Tom� e Principe (RSTP), often taped in the courtyard outside at night, and released on cassette or occasionally, vinyl. It captures the joy of post-1975 independence and only fizzled out as styles changed and musicians struggled to make ends meet. Yet, take a quick listen to recent RSTP programming, which features musicians such as Babilonia or Calema, and you�ll still hear Puxa rhythms, showing just how potent the music form this two-island nation is on a global level. And Bongo Joe, who have also released two volumes featuring the above mentioned Africa Negra, have given this music the treatment it deserves, with extensive notes on the country�s history, vintage photographs, and band discographies. items.body: Those of us who have been digging into Analog Africa�s increasingly formidable releases over the last two decades are well aware of the massive amount of raw, vodun-based Sato and Sakpata-derived funk the label has issued by Benin�s most prolific 1970s-era band, the Orchestre Poly-Ritmo. AA has dropped no fewer than 3 compilations of their heaviest material, as well as a reissue of the band�s first LP, in an effort to give them the international status they deserve. That being said, what might be different about this collection of their music? And who is Antoine Dougb�? Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa As it turns out, Dougb� was a song-conjurer whose mode of musical transfer was slapping his legs in a rhythm known as Cavacha, a groove created by drummer Belobi Meridjo, who was inspired by a train cadence that he worked into a pattern that ultimately spread like a 21st century California wildfire throughout Congolese pop music in the mid-1970s. Dougb�, known as the �Devil�s Prime Minister,� was also a practitioner of vodun who inspired fear in any musician he felt was unsuited to play his music, which is how he landed on working exclusively Poly-Ritmo, as he felt they could nail what he wanted in ways other bands couldn�t. His recording career was brief - 3 albums and a few singles - but as this collection shows, it was potent. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa Because of the era from which this music dates, it�s not surprising that the recording and instrument tones have changed - the guitars have a plastic sheen and synthesizers appear- even if the music remains rooted in the 1970s. Perhaps the influence of the Cuban son is more apparent here than on other Poly-Ritmo collections, especially in the collection�s initial offerings. And yes, Congolese rumba, then shaking all of sub-Saharan Africa to its knees, is present too. �Ma Won Min Towe Leo� is one example. Opening with a bed of synthesizers, the shimmering guitars, tinny, seemingly squeezed dry by the 80s themselves, lock in over relentless high-hat-focused grooves. The guitars finally start firing in different directions midway through, before that synth weaves back in, forming a bed underneath it all. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa �We Tayi Sin Assi Tche� is much more overtly Cuban. With its insistent cowbell, classic, nasal vocal call and response, and tight, repeated guitar figures, its debt to mid-twentieth century Afro-Cuban sons is transparent. Another track, �Djomido Ma Dougbe Tche� rides a groove reminiscent of 70�s-era Franco classic �Liberte.� The pulse is relentless, and the guitar solo repeats a tight repetition of a few notes, driving listeners to ecstasy all the while. However, none of this music is a mere copy of its influences; rather, like so much potent pop coming from the continent at the time, it is a swirl of major influences rendered by local rhythms and vocal phrasing to give it specific identity, in this case, to Benin. Dougb�s musical role on this collection is a bit murky. One of his three albums has a photo of him, fully mic�d behind a collection of hand drums, so perhaps he served as a percussionist/vocalist; this release never explains. He wasn�t a songwriter in the traditional sense. It seems he was more of an instigator and arranger, but his thumbprint was apparently heavy enough to warrant his name on the records he was involved with. Whatever the case, in his brief run as a recording artist, he and Poly-Ritmo produced a handful of driving, Cavacha-inspired grooves that can still wear holes in club floors. Further reading: Petrona Mart�nez - Ancestras (Review) Gnonnas Pedro & His Dadjes - Roi De L'Agbadja Moderne 1974-1983 (Review)

items._cn_summary: 本辑收录贝宁传奇乐队Orchestre Poly-Rythmo与作曲家Antoine Dougbé于1977至1982年间合作的作品。Dougbé以击打大腿演绎Cavacha节奏著称，该节奏由鼓手Belobi Meridjo受火车节拍启发而创，后广泛传播于刚果流行乐中。作为伏都教实践者，Dougbé仅与Poly-Rythmo长期合作，认为唯有此乐队能精准呈现其构想。乐评指出，相较于此前几张厂牌合辑，本作的古巴son影响更为明显，尤其在开篇曲目中表现突出；同时刚果伦巴元素亦贯穿其中。制作层面受时代录音条件所限，吉他带有塑料质感音色，合成器亦开始出现，与根植于七十年代的律动形成有趣对话。Analog Africa作为专注非洲音乐再版的小厂牌持续挖掘贝宁乐队的深层档案，此辑为研究西非放克与拉丁跨界提供了新的文本。

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?

items._cn_summary: 这是丹麦三人组合GuldGanger的首张数字EP，包含五首曲目，由北欧民谣圈资深主唱Mia Guldhammer领衔。大部分曲目基于传统素材，乐队成员各自带来不同诠释，专辑整体笼罩在一种古朴而略带粗粝的氛围中。开场曲以奔跑般的律动展示主唱富有说服力的声线；唯一原创曲目由成员Morten Musicus创作，融合口簧与风笛形成持续推进的动力。传统曲目中，钦巴龙琴提供了细腻的织体背景，口簧的柔和运用增添了乐器之间的层次。最后一首器乐曲以弹性节奏开场，融合长笛与弦乐，产生一种令人振奋且略带失衡感的声响效果。五首曲目展现了一个似乎已经相当成熟与有实力的乐队起点，为后续全长专辑留下了期待空间。

items.body: Kr�ta , the latest release on Norway's Taragot label, features a Swede and two Norwegians playing interpretations of mainly traditional tunes from their respective countries. Fiddler Mats Ed�n has long been involved in Swedish folk music, as a player, composer and teacher, and in the process exploring and integrating different musical styles and approaches. Tellef Kvifte was in the pioneering Norwegian crossover band Slinkombas in the 1970s and has continued to play a central role in Norwegian folk music, both as a musician and an academic. Most often heard playing the sj�fl�yte , more widely known as a recorder, Kvifte has employed other instruments from outside the Norwegian tradition, in particular the saxophone and bagpipes. His son Knut Kvifte Nesheim , a drummer and composer, has also shown a determination to blur the lines between different musical genres, both in his solo and group projects. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio It comes as no surprise then to find this trio offering a far from conventional take on the tunes they have chosen. While dance tunes may be the source of most of the material here, this feels more akin to chamber music; not that it is remotely classical in style, but in the sense it conveys of three players engrossed in a musically intimate conversation. This is not a performance appropriate for accompanying dancers but might instead be seen as an exploration of hidden possibilities of meaning in the music. In so doing it reveals some of its underlying mystery, including, perhaps, a darker side. Just as in an Ibsen play, where the surface bonhomie, jollity and social nicety can be hiding something more sinister, in Scandinavian dance music there are at times hints of a troublesome undercurrent below the surface. So the decision to open proceedings with �Fossgrimen,� a fiddle tune from Norway's Setesdal valley, is perhaps significant. A fossgrimen is a mythical creature, a kind of water-sprite living in waterfalls from whom fiddle-players were considered to have learned their skills and for that were not universally welcomed, with the fiddle considered to be the devil's instrument. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio Tellef Kvifte takes the lead melody on most tracks but on the Swedish �Polska from Per Myhr,� having played a repeated introductory riff on the sj�fl�yte, with Mats Ed�n providing an amorphous textural accompaniment below and Nesheim adding some quiet tinkling, it's Ed�n who introduces the tune on the fiddle with Kvifte proceeding to play in unison. It's a short track and almost as soon as it gets going things start to fragment and everything grind to a halt.

items.body: Winter Sect will release “Graveyard Girl” on October 2, 2026 on Bandcamp and streaming platforms, a new single from the Washington, D.C. goth rock band’s upcoming EP, “Offering.” The track follows “Say Goodbye,” released earlier in 2026. The sound of ‘Graveyard Girl’ Where “Say Goodbye” leaned into darker territory, “Graveyard Girl” keeps its post-punk backbone but loosens up, pulling in funk bass lines, garage grit, indie pop hooks and a touch of bossa nova rhythm. Singer, lyricist and keyboardist Heather Wayward said the song came together almost by accident during a rehearsal setup: “The song pretty much started with Claudia grooving out on a bass line. It was catchy and I thought let’s do something completely different and not so serious and macabre. First the hook was discovered and we built from there. So with that funk of a groove my mind started walking. Where? Through the graveyard of course. It came together in a cool way and a little twist at the end just makes it fun.” About Winter Sect Winter Sect was formed in late 2023 by California native Claudia Neuman and guitarist Anthony Piazza, both members of DC/Baltimore post-punk band Sister Ex, to pursue a feedback-drenched sound spanning goth, new wave, industrial and psychedelic music with a dark, theatrical rock presentation. The lineup is rounded out by Heather Wayward on keys and vocals and drummer Darryl J. Dardenne, with Neuman also on bass and vocals. The band released two singles, “Mystic Twin” and “Haunted House,” in 2024, followed by “Say Goodbye” in 2026. “Graveyard Girl” will appear on the band’s upcoming EP, “Offering.”

items.body: This Mortal Coil, the rotating collective of musicians and vocalists assembled by 4AD founder Ivo Watts-Russell, released its second studio album, “Filigree & Shadow,” on 22 September 1986 through 4AD. The double LP turns 40 this year. The album gathered 25 tracks, about half of them instrumental, credited to This Mortal Coil but built around a different set of contributors than the project’s 1984 debut. Ivo Watts-Russell and producer John Fryer recorded and mixed “Filigree & Shadow” at Blackwing and Palladium Studios, with arrangements from Simon Raymonde of Cocteau Twins, cellist Martin McCarrick and engineer John Turner, plus violin and viola from Gini Ball. Dead Can Dance percussionist Peter Ulrich and members of Dif Juz, The Wolfgang Press and Colourbox also appeared on the record. Vocalists including Dominic Appleton of Breathless and Alison Limerick sang cover interpretations of songs by Tim Buckley, Gene Clark, Van Morrison, Colin Newman and Talking Heads. “Filigree & Shadow” reached number 53 on the UK Albums Chart and number 2 on the UK Indie Chart, and it streams on Spotify. About This Mortal Coil Ivo Watts-Russell founded 4AD in London in 1980 and built This Mortal Coil a few years later to record music outside the constraints of a fixed band. In 1983 he brought together Cocteau Twins’ Elizabeth Fraser and Robin Guthrie, Cindytalk’s Gordon Sharp and members of Modern English to re-record two Modern English songs as the medley “Sixteen Days/Gathering Dust.” Its B-side, a cover of Tim Buckley’s “Song to the Siren” sung by Fraser and Guthrie alone, entered the UK Singles Chart at number 66 and led Watts-Russell to build a full album around the same idea. That album, “It’ll End in Tears,” followed in 1984 on 4AD. This Mortal Coil never had a fixed lineup. Watts-Russell and engineer John Fryer were its only constant members, and each record drew on a different group of musicians and singers, most pulled from 4AD’s own roster. “Filigree & Shadow” followed in 1986 as the project’s second album, again produced by Watts-Russell and Fryer, with Simon Raymonde, Martin McCarrick and Gini Ball forming its core backing group and Peter Ulrich among the guest musicians. This Mortal Coil closed its studio run with “Blood” in 1991, on which vocalist Caroline Crawley – whose death Side-Line reported in 2016 – was among the featured singers. After the group’s run ended, Watts-Russell continued the same collaborative approach under the name The Hope Blister from 1998, while Fryer went on to produce and engineer widely across the 4AD roster and beyond. “Filigree & Shadow” turns 40 this year, four decades into a project that treated an album as a collaboration rather than the work of a fixed band.
items._genre: dream pop / ethereal / post-punk / darkwave
items._cn_summary: 本文纪念This Mortal Coil第二张专辑《Filigree & Shadow》发行40周年。这张1986年的双张LP由4AD创始人Ivo Watts-Russell策划，是没有固定阵容的合奏项目，集合了Cocteau Twins、Dif Juz、Dead Can Dance等厂牌旗下乐手参与录制。专辑包含25首曲目，约半数为器乐作品，融合了大提琴、小提琴、中提琴等古典乐器配置，编曲由Simon Raymonde、Martin McCarrick等人完成。演唱者包括Breathless主唱Dominic Appleton和Alison Limerick，翻唱了Tim Buckley、Van Morrison、Talking Heads等创作者的作品。专辑在英国专辑榜排名第53，独立榜排名第2。文章后半段回顾了This Mortal Coil的起源，从1983年翻唱Tim Buckley《Song to the Siren》开始，到1991年以《Blood》结束，随后Watts-Russell以The Hope Blister延续了类似的合作模式。本文属于纪念性新闻报道，缺乏深度评论。

items.body: Review by Finnforest — A Charming Entrance Salis was a band from Sardinia named for the two Salis brothers, Antonio and Francesco. They wouldrelease three albums in the 1970s and be yet another inhabitant of that deep RPI back bench. Farbeyond the many well-known classic Italian pop/rock bands getting respect and attention on thesurface, there were so many other bands who never made the front bench. Even many prog fans whoembrace the existence of RPI may not have heard of a band like Salis. And yet, so many of theseobscure groups have work that is worthy of attention even if it is not the full-blown progressiverock that would follow later in the decade.While most people will point to their "proggiest" third album, it is the this debut that is of mostinterest to me. It joins a crucial group of Italian proto-RPI bands who set the stage for what wascoming just around the bend. This group of bands ranges from Italian pop to blues rock to psychrock, all pushing the barriers of their own zone while releasing work that was not quite fullyformed progressive rock. Some are just okay and some are quite exciting. This is one of the betterones in my view. While you have the short song format and bluesy-jazzy psych rock variations, theirsecret weapon is their passion and an amazing feel for memorable little motifs that are not alwayspredictable. They begin to seep into your head after just a couple spins, and I think it may besttheir other two releases that get most of the attention. This first Salis album is a must for RPIfans who like stuff like Fabio Celi, Il Mucchio, and Equipe 84. Sometimes the special sauce is justyouth.
items._genre: Italian progressive rock / proto-prog / psych rock
items._cn_summary: SALIS 是来自撒丁岛的兄弟二人组合，1971年首张专辑属于意大利前卫摇滚的早期萌芽阶段。乐评将其归入 RPI 后排乐队行列，介于意大利流行、布鲁斯摇滚与迷幻摇滚之间，尚未完全进化为成熟的前卫摇滚形态。专辑采用短曲式结构，融合爵士化与布鲁斯化的迷幻变奏，核心亮点在于乐手的创作激情与出人意料的动机片段——这些旋律碎片在反复聆听后会逐渐渗入听者记忆。乐评认为这张处女作在同类型作品中属于较佳水准，甚至优于乐队后来被更多关注的第三张专辑。对于喜爱 Fabio Celi、Il Mucchio、Equipe 84 等意大利早期前卫萌芽乐队的听众而言，这是一张值得发掘的遗珠。

items.body: Review by toroddreincarnated — The second album from this band from Norway.The band was a duo with a line-up of double bass, bass, guitars, keyboards, concertina, effects andvocals.A number of guests added drums, violins, strings and trumpet.This is the follow-up album to their 2024 debut album Bridge Of Sighs from 2024. An album I reviewedback in April 2024 in # 3 of my blog The Sound Of Fighting Cats. I gave it a three stars review.Lullabies for the Marooned clocks in at three quarters of an hour.The music here is art-rock.The band, I mean duo, has retreated from the more rocking soundscape on their debut album into amuch more intimate, softly spoken and refined soundscape on their new album, the follow-up album.Early Genesis, Procol Harum, Sylvan, Talk Talk and Peter Hammill are good references here. There areeven some Steve Hogarth era Marillion lurking around in their music too. There is a blend of acoustic and electric instruments here, including guitars. The strings is addinga lot of colours and are complementing the great vocals.This is an album where a piece of music crosses over to becoming an artwork. The result is a great album and one of this year's better albums from Norway, the new powerhouse inart-rock and prog rock. 4 stars

items.body: Zadisphere, an independent dark ritual techno project, published the video “Cathedral” on its official YouTube channel on September 9, 2026. Zadisphere makes a sound that mixes dark ritual techno with cinematic electronics and hypnotic rhythms, combining gothic and baroque elements, pipe organs, strings and choirs with analog sequences. “Cathedral” is a standalone video release; no tied single, EP or label has been confirmed. Zadisphere’s ‘Cathedral’ follows a steady run of new tracks “Cathedral” arrived in a run of near-weekly uploads from the project through August and September 2026, including “Czas / Time” on August 12, “Monolith Threshold” on September 1, “Ritual” on September 3, a remix of Ludwik Sempoliński’s “Ten wąsik” on September 11, “Nienazwane / Unnamed” on September 14 and “Po drugiej stronie / The other side” on September 16. No tracklist, formats or streaming availability have been confirmed for “Cathedral” beyond the YouTube upload. About Zadisphere Behind Zadisphere is a solo artist who treats mood and atmosphere as the project’s real subject, with sound built to serve that focus rather than the other way around. Its stated direction combines dark ritual techno, cinematic electronics and hypnotic rhythms with gothic and baroque influences, using pipe organs, strings, choirs and analog sequences. The project’s YouTube channel was created in January 2024, but its run of released tracks and videos began in August 2026 with “Czas / Time”, followed within weeks by “Monolith Threshold”, “Ritual” and “Cathedral”. Zadisphere has no confirmed label, Discogs entry or Wikipedia page. The project is also present on Instagram and maintains an official website. “Cathedral” is its latest video release.

items.body: Black Tape For A Blue Girl and Projekt Records reissue “The Rope” on October 2, presenting the 1986 debut album in a limited edition that pairs the original mix, remastered, with a new 2026 mix by Sam Rosenthal for its 40th anniversary. The 2LP edition is limited to 300 copies on 140-gram vinyl, with LP1 pressed on baby blue vinyl with black splatters and LP2 on transparent blue vinyl with white splatters. A 2CD digipak edition adds seven bonus tracks. Both formats are released via Projekt Records. “The Rope” is Black Tape For A Blue Girl’s debut album, the project Sam Rosenthal built around his songwriting and electronics, with Oscar Herrera on vocals. Each format includes the full 12-track album twice: the original 1986 mix, remastered, and the new 2026 mix. Martin Bowes of Attrition handled the mastering. The 2LP package adds a 16-page lyric and memorabilia fanzine insert plus a sticker; the 2CD edition comes in a 6-panel digipak with a 4-panel photo insert and sticker. The original 1986 tracklist runs: “memory, uncaring friend”, “hide in yourself”, “within these walls”, “the holy terrors”, “end”, “seven days til sunrise”, “the rope”, “the few remaining threads”, “the lingering flicker”, “slow blur”, “the floor was hard but home” and “we return”. The 2CD edition adds seven bonus tracks exclusive to that format: “the lingering flicker (first draft)”, “within these walls (early mix with clarinet)”, “the holy terrors (long)”, “second dream”, “the lingering flicker (isolated violins)”, “within these walls (short with violins)” and “memory, uncaring friend (remix intro)”. Sam Rosenthal on writing ‘The Rope’ Black Tape For A Blue Girl’s Rosenthal, who also founded Projekt Records, described the circumstances that produced the album: “In November ’85, following two years of recording instrumental electronic music, I invited Oscar Herrera to sing two songs on my ISLANDS cassette. A few months later in February of ’86 I left Florida for college in Orange, California. I was 20 years old, feeling isolated, lonely, missing friends back home. In my dorm room that spring I used the school’s Fostex 250 4-track cassette portastudio to record songs with my lyrics and melodies. Writing words for Oscar to sing over my ethereal and ambient music helped me explore those angsty and tangled feelings. The Rope is half vocal and half instrumental. It’s all quite minimal, yet it’s an album listeners still mention as a favorite. Capturing the confusion and darkness I felt at that time remains valid; new listeners connect with it today. I never would have expected that 40 years later The Rope would be listened to and appreciated by new generations. It’s really nice knowing those feelings are timeless, and the music has a place in people’s lives.” Uncut included “The Rope” in its “200 Greatest Goth Albums” feature, describing it as: “The vehicle for the more electronic songwriting of Projekt Records’ founder Sam Rosenthal, brought to life by singer Oscar Herrera’s arch delivery. BTFABG spun a unique thread of ambient darkwave, neoclassical exoticism and dark cabaret on their relatively bare-boned and lo-fi debut album.” The Rope (40th) by Black Tape For A Blue Girl About Black Tape For A Blue Girl Black Tape For A Blue Girl is the project Sam Rosenthal formed in 1986, built around his own songwriting and electronics and centered from the start on the pairing of his instrumental, ambient compositions with vocalists singing his lyrics. “The Rope”, released that year on Projekt Records, the label Rosenthal founded, introduced Oscar Herrera as vocalist alongside contributions from Allan Kraut, Kim Prior, Adam Buhler, Candy Sherlock and Lara Radford. The project’s discography continued through “Mesmerized by the Sirens” (1987), “Ashes in the Brittle Air” (1989), “A Chaos of Desire” (1991), “This Lush Garden Within” (1993), “Remnants of a Deeper Purity” (1996), “As One Aflame Laid Bare by Desire” (1999), “The Scavenger Bride” (2002), “Halo Star” (2004), “10 Neurotics” (2009), “Tenderotics” (2013), “These Fleeting Moments” (2016), “To Touch the Milky Way” (2018) and “The Cleft Serpent” (2021). Projekt has revisited several of these titles as anniversary reissues in recent years, including “The Cleft Serpent” and “Ashes in the Brittle Air” on vinyl, “Mesmerized by the Sirens” on vinyl and double CD, and “As One Aflame Laid Bare by Desire” and “Remnants of a Deeper Purity” in their own anniversary editions. Rosenthal has also continued to release music outside the project, including ambient and drone recordings under his own name. The 40th anniversary edition of “The Rope” extends that reissue campaign to the album that started it, presenting Herrera’s original vocal performances and Rosenthal’s 1986 arrangements alongside his 2026 revisiting of the same material.

items.body: Room of Wires, the UK industrial/electronic duo of two producers who both go by Andrew, released the single “Skin weevil” on September 18, 2026, self-released on Bandcamp. The two-track release pairs the title track with “Do not leave a message” and arrives while the duo works on a new album. Skin weevil by Room of Wires Room of Wires bring an industrial and electronic sound that mixes hard-hitting rhythm programming with the duo’s usual dark ambient textures and field recordings. Both tracks on “Skin weevil” were written and produced by Room of Wires; the cover artwork is by the duo as well, with performance for camera by Fenia Kotsopoulou and photography by Daz Disley. Room of Wires’ ‘Skin weevil’ single The duo has not met in person: one member works with hardware and a tangle of physical wires, the other in software and virtual cables, sharing ideas and sounds over the internet. That process has produced “Skin weevil” as a standalone two-track single rather than part of a longer EP or album, released independently while the pair continue work on their next full-length. No further tracks or release date for that album have been announced. About Room of Wires Room of Wires is a UK industrial/electronic duo of two producers, both named Andrew, who write and record without ever having met, exchanging sounds and ideas remotely. Their debut EP, “Asylum sneaker”, appeared on Section27 in August 2014, followed by the Bandcamp-only “Dead skins” EP in November 2015, “Used as a runner” on Section27 in June 2016, “Black medicine” on Section27 in June 2017, and the remix-featuring “Mastakink” EP, self-released in October 2017. Their debut album, “White transit”, followed in November 2018, and the mini-LP “Test subject” arrived in October 2019. Room of Wires signed to the German label ant-zen for the albums “Plague of people” (April 2021) and “Welcome to the end game” (February 2023), releasing the “Fever switch” EP on Rednetic in October 2021 in between. Further self-released EPs followed with “Floodplains” (November 2023) and the album “If no other means are effective” in December 2025, the duo’s first full-length in close to three years. Alongside their own catalogue, Room of Wires record collaborative material as DasF and Cave like carving, and have contributed remixes and tracks to releases by Ah Cama-Sotz, Flint Glass, 4T Thieves and other acts. “Skin weevil” is their first new material since 2025’s “If no other means are effective”, released as the pair continue work on a new Room of Wires album.

items.body: Karine Polwart has proved herself to be an exceptional talent as a singer and songwriter for many years, all the way back to her time with Malinky (the song �Thaney� was a revelation). As a solo artist she�s grown and continually expanded her horizons, coming now to Windblown , a project that began life seven years ago, when Polwart, along with sound designer and composer Pippa Murphy, was artist in residence at Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh. The album, with its stage show and book, tells the story of the garden�s oldest specimen, a Sabal palm tree ( Sabal bermudana ), which was gently felled in 2021, and contained a surprise nobody had expected. The tree is the starting point. From there, imagination runs free. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan It�s an album of voice and piano (the outstanding, sympathetic Dave Milligan), and, for all its global outlook on connections, one that�s very rooted in Scotland. You can hear it on the opening track, �Hear The Rigging/Last In Line,� where the melody becomes a slow, aching lament that would sound completely natural on the pipes. The stripped-down sound gives the songs both crafted stateliness and real intimacy. Each one is an exhalation, a memory, a celebration and exploration, with recurring phrases in the words and music acting as touchstones � or even hooks; they certainly stick in the mind. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan In many ways, this is a modest album, with piano, voice and light, judicious soundscaping. It won�t overpower with noise. Yet at the same time, it�s epic, a look at history, at the flow and grandeur of nature, and the things we all carry within us. The music, and especially Polwart�s warm, compassionate voice, envelop the listener, and makes them a participant, not an observer, but a part of the journey and the history. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan The irony arrives at the end, when the venerable old tree is down, and seeds are examined. What people for two hundred years had believed to be a Sabal bermudana turns out to be something different, a Sabal mexicana � and one of the small plants fill grow where it�s forerunner once stood. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan Like music, plants keep to a different time � and this album/book/show give the tree the requiem it deserves, as well as hope for the future. items.body:
According to its founder, Eugene Rodriguez, who also sings and plays on the record, Los Cenzontles is a �musical group and non-profit organization, which I founded over thirty years ago.�  As he continues in the album�s liner notes, the group �has a long history of producing projects exploring Mexico�s deep roots and our connections with various traditions that, so far, have included Irish, Louisiana Creole, Cuban, American cowboy, classical, pop, rock, and blues�, the latest of which is
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�

items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items.body: In August 1819, tens of thousands of working men and women gathered in St. Peter�s Field in Manchester to hear the politician Henry Hunt speak. They were difficult times, many still out of work after the Napoleonic wars, rising prices and low wages � and always those at the bottom of the heap suffering. Hunt was a famed orator, a man on the side of the people, able to stir and inspire with his voice. Although the gathering was peaceful, the size of the crowd terrified the magistrates, who panicked and imagined an uprising. They sent in half-trained dragoons and the cavalry, who rode down, slashed and killed without compunction or compassion. In the end, 18 died and up to 700 were wounded. It was a stain on the nation, an outrage; prompting Percy Shelley, one of the poetic giants of the age, to write The Masque of Anarchy , with its famous lines: �Rise like Lions after slumber / in unvanquishable number / She your chains to earth like dew / Which in sleep had fallen on you / Ye are many - they are few.� Peterloo, as people called it, remains one of the seminal events in English working-class history, one that Sean Cooney of the Young 'Uns has revisited for this album of original songs, which is lavishly presented in a book with contemporary letters, political cartoons and illustrations to create a multimedia event. It�s ambitious, no doubt about that, and he�s selected some great talent to help � guitarist Sam Carter, the almost ubiquitous fiddler/singer Eliza Carthy, Ben Nicholls supplying background and texture on various instruments, and the Lancashire industrial ballad singer Jennifer Reid, who doubles as narrator. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid For a small ensemble, they make a powerful noise. The songs capture the feel of the day; the anticipation and excitement at the summer gathering, the joy that turns to terror and flight as the troops charge, then the bitter, mournful aftermath, voiced some powerful melodies and very well-chosen images. As a writer, Cooney often focuses on the personal in the small tales of people like �Sam Bamford� and �Mary Fildes,� while the three short pieces that comprise �The Monkey Rides The Mare� capture the bluster and arrogance of the soldiers. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid Cooney is a persuasive singer, and on this heartfelt project, he puts plenty of emotion into his voice. Having two other outstanding vocalists alongside him makes for a wonderful triple threat. In these days when governments across the world are cracking down on protest, this stands as a sobering and very timely reminder. It�s a history lesson, yes, but the detail of the history stays in the book, while the music creates a set of songs that will resonate and remain for a long time. Find the artist online. items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以1819年曼彻斯特圣彼得广场大屠杀为题材，通过原创歌曲重现这一英国工人阶级历史事件。Sean Cooney邀请了多位音乐人参与，包括歌手兼小提琴家Eliza Carthy、吉他手Sam Carter等，形成了一支小型但声音有力的乐团。专辑以书籍形式呈现，收录同时代信件、政治漫画和插图，构成一种多媒体体验。歌词聚焦于个人故事，如Sam Bamford和Mary Fildes等具体人物，捕捉集会当天的期待、兴奋、恐惧与悲痛。部分曲目如《The Monkey Rides The Mare》以三段短曲刻画士兵的虚张声势与傲慢。作为概念专辑，它既是历史课也是音乐作品，在当下全球政府压制抗议的背景下具有现实意义。

items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."
items._genre: field recording / spoken word / soundscape
items._cn_summary: 这是一张由录音师Ian Brennan在芝加哥南区的街头采集的田野录音专辑，并非传统意义上的音乐作品。二十五名遭受枪支暴力影响的社区居民参与了录制，年龄从十七岁到六十七岁不等，他们在前廊上讲述自己的亲身经历，偶尔穿插即兴说唱。录音地点选在一位九十四岁祖母的住宅前，位于中途机场降落航线下方。编辑以编者的形式呈现，强调这不是评论而是现实本身的记录。项目收益将捐给Cure Violence Global。这一作品更偏向声音艺术与社区档案的范畴，制作理念强调零添加、纯粹环境采集，跨越了音乐、社会学与纪实听觉的边界。

items.body: Review by sgtpepper — Alan Parsons Project continued with their prolific album production in 1979. Despite the concept album being out of favour in the time of more superficial music styles (disco, punk) the band holds on to what they do best - clever songwriting, a couple of well arranged instrumentals and heart-broken ballads. "The Lucifer" offers a promising mildly progressive start loaded with synths. The funky "You lie down with dogs" follows, splendid vocal harmonies and live instrumentation. "I'd rather be a man" is the hardest rocking and loudest song on this release. My main interests in this song lie in the rhythm section (bass). "You won't be there" is a melancholic track which would suit to any post-Beatle 70's output but mainly George.After that, the output gets less memorable and unique, for 2 or songs yet it remains pleasant. "Don't hold back" is a simple catchy pop song.But now we're coming to the brilliant two tracks - the Beach Boys magic loaded "Secret gardens", an instrumental with the melody as strong as the sweeping vocal arrangements and atmosphere a la Pet Sounds. After this level of sophistication, we're faced by one of the strongest APP ballads with dreamy melancholic lyrics and fitting music underscoring the message.Lesley Duncan vocal was a great choice as was the mighty church organ chords which evoke the sense of helplessness in me.Recommended to fans of progressive and well executed pop.
items._genre: crossover prog / art pop / soft rock
items._cn_summary: Alan Parsons Project延续其高产的专辑制作路线，在迪斯科与朋克盛行的1979年坚持概念专辑的形式。专辑以合成器铺陈的前卫开场，融入放克节奏与强劲贝斯线条，后段呈现受披头士后期影响的忧郁民谣气质。器乐曲目'神秘花园'以人声和声与管风琴和弦营造出Pet Sounds式的氛围质感，被视为专辑最出色的段落之一。Lesley Duncan的人声与教堂风琴相结合，强化了歌曲中关于无助感的情绪表达。整体而言，这是一张制作精良、旋律优美但实验性有限的概念专辑，适合渐进摇滚与精致流行乐爱好者，但距离真正的前卫实验领域仍有相当距离。

items.body: Review by brainsuccasurgery — The surname Gildenl'w is by no means unfamiliar to us. There's no need to explain why here. But it might be worth dwelling a bit on his first name. Born in Sweden, Kristoffer was the bassist for Pain of Salvation up until the double album *Be* (2004), and like most bassists, his demeanor was more low-key at the time, and his role seemingly less prominent than that of his brother, the frontman. Can we then speak of emancipation? Or simply of a search for another form of personal fulfillment? In any case, in 2003, at the height of the famous progressive metal band's popularity, Kristoffer left Sweden and Pain of Salvation to move to the Netherlands, collaborating on both sides of the Atlantic with some heavyweights of the progressive rock scene (Damien Wilson, Neal Morse, Lana Lane, the band Kayak'), before launching a solo career in 2012 with the album *Rust*.Begun in 2019 (alongside the album *Homebound*), *Empty*, Kristoffer Gildenl'w's fifth and latest solo album, was originally scheduled for 2020, but a devastating pandemic had other plans, and an unexpected *Let Me Be A Ghost* took precedence, releasing in 2021. Despite its overarching theme (depression), the album *Let Me Be A Ghost* still contained beautiful moments of musical serenity, a touch of melodic and harmonic lightness, as if weightless. There was gravity, too, but it knew how to be playful at times. And this ghostly imprint ultimately led to a kind of peace. 'Let Me Be A Ghost' seemed to describe the sensation of falling'but a fall from which one gets back up, with difficulty, not without effort, yet with courage and the feeling of having grown.'Empty' is even more striking because it offers a broader critical perspective on another tragic fall'that of humanity, drawn into the emptiness of our existence. The music thus becomes the anxious echo of a palpable despair that conveys the state of mind of a man struggling not to fall into this void'this vast, searing void that weighs on our hearts, terrified at the thought of what humanity is doing, a lost humanity in search of meaning.Like his previous solo albums, *Empty* possesses the same strange power of attraction'an irresistible pull that draws us entirely into a universe poised between dream and reality, between soothing light and revealing darkness. How can one resist lyrics so beautiful, so poignant'all these words that soar directly toward the heavens, sung in that deep, comforting, instantly recognizable voice that speaks of disarray, doubt, the pain of incomprehension in the face of human beings' self-destructive recklessness'a voice that speaks to us of our fears and sufferings as fragile beings, just as one might speak to a damned soul waiting in vain for its due.Despite all, one senses the presence of a mystery'a reflection on our purpose in life'carried by Kristoffer Gildenl'w's music and the brilliant artists who perform it. Each composition is a bewildering showcase of beauty, set to restrained vocals, but that is precisely what makes Kristoffer's style so powerful and heightens the emotional vertigo it evokes in us. Each track on his album is a profound and expansive anthem that can help us endure all the torments of the world. We can sense echoes of his former band. We can sense his love for Joni Mitchell, Mike Oldfield, and other giants of the '70s. We hear echoes of Anathema or Dire Straits. We encounter heart-wrenching blues ' la Pink Floyd, the kind whose mysteries were known only to Gilmour and Waters when they were still able to get along. It is dark and dense music, yet it regularly lightens, expands, shakes itself free, moves, and brightens'notably thanks to the graceful arabesques of Ben Mathot and Anne Bakker's violins, a rhythm section capable of softening its touch, the enchanting piano arpeggios played by Kristoffer himself, or the memorable feverish surges of the electric guitar tamed by sorcerers who seem to command the waves and the flames; all these warm notes like so many stars burning eternally to soothe our nights.*Empty* is one of those rich and profound progressive rock works that give us all the more the more we bring of ourselves to them as we receive them'intuitively felt by the heart yet always surprising to the ear. By giving us the best of himself here'which requires great courage' Kristoffer Gildenl'w sets an example by casting an intense light into the night of our troubled souls, illuminating with irrepressible hope a reality before which the malevolent structures of our destructive imagination and our death-dealing impulses dissolve'the only true light, the one that seeks to purify us of our unforgivable sins committed against Mother Nature. In the end, 'Empty' is neither sad nor despairing. In any case, even in the face of impending disaster, there will always be something good to take away'if only a tiny drop of happiness or a pinch of love.
items._genre: crossover prog / progressive rock / art rock
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是瑞典音乐人Kristoffer Gildenlöw的第五张个人作品，主题围绕空虚感与人类存在意义的失落展开。前Pain of Salvation贝斯手在离开乐队后转往荷兰发展，延续了跨界前卫摇滚的创作路线。乐评描述其音乐在梦境与现实、安抚之光与揭示之暗之间游走，歌词富有诗性，嗓音低沉且具有辨识度。评论指出每首作品都展现了令人困惑的美感，整体氛围类似对人类自我毁灭倾向的焦虑回响。然而从风格来看，该作品属于主流跨界前卫摇滚范畴，未触及深度实验、爵士或电子等用户偏好的领域，融合度有限，制作偏向传统前卫摇滚乐队编制。乐评本身较长且富有文采，但音乐本身的创新性与用户口味匹配度较低。

items.body: Black Sherif takes his own sound apart on SUN SHERIF, the six-track EP he released through Blacko Management and EMPIRE in early September. The Konongo-born singer and rapper calls it “a deconstruction of everything Black Sherif’s done sonically“, a method that gives him the obsession he says he needs when working through fifteen or twenty demos at a time. That sound took shape on the “First Sermon” and “Second Sermon” singles of 2021, Twi verses set over highlife melody and UK drill drums, and in 2022 “Kwaku the Traveller” carried it to number one on Apple Music in Ghana and Nigeria. Two albums followed, The Villain I Never Was in 2022 and Iron Boy in April 2025. The EP brings in the Ghanaian singer AratheJay on “Forever” and the Trinidadian production duo Full Blown on “Love Again”, and Sherif sings “Jolie” alone, moving between Twi and English towards a chorus built on the French word for pretty. The verses are made of small acts of devotion: a New Year’s drive to her door, songs written for her in the manner of Kurt Cobain, a habit dropped because she disliked it. Listen to “Jolie” HERE and stream SUN SHERIF following THIS LINK The post Daily Discovery: Black Sherif – Jolie appeared first on Rhythm Passport.
items._genre: afrobeats / hiplife / UK drill fusion / highlife
items._cn_summary: 这篇文章聚焦于加纳歌手兼说唱艺人 Black Sherif 于2025年9月发行的六曲EP，介绍其如何对自己既有声线进行"解构式"回溯。EP延续了他以特威语演唱搭配高生活旋律与英国 drill 鼓点的标志性配方，合作阵容包括加纳歌手 AratheJay 与特立尼达制作组合 Full Blown。文章用较大篇幅梳理了艺人的职业轨迹，从2021年的"First Sermon"与"Second Sermon"单曲讲起，经2022年登顶加纳与尼日利亚苹果音乐的"Kwaku the Traveller"，直至两张录音室专辑及本张EP。标题曲"Jolie"以特威语与英语交替展开，副歌借法语"漂亮"之意构筑情感核心，歌词围绕驾车夜访、为恋人创作歌曲、戒除对方不喜欢的习惯等亲密细节展开，是一首以情感叙事驱动的流行向作品。

items.body: Norwegian synthpop act Echo Image is entering the final phase of work on its new album, “My Shadow, My Echo and Me.” Pål-Magnus Rybom, the musician behind the project, has now listened to the record from beginning to end for the first time, describing the experience as “strange but pretty damn good.” The record has been in the making for close to 20 years, with only final mixing, mastering and the artwork still to complete. No release date has been announced yet. The album follows Echo Image’s return with the singles “Walk My Mind” (2021), “Mono No Aware” (2022), “Of Truth” (2023) and “Madsong” (2024), material that gradually marked the project’s way back after a long period of relative silence following its 2002 split. Rybom has linked each word in the title to a stage of his own story: the Shadow for what still weighs on him, the Echo for the music that got him through it, and Me for who he is now on the other side of it. The project involves several names from the Norwegian electronic scene. Apoptygma Berzerk‘s Stephan Groth, whose Pitch Black Drive label has released Echo Image’s comeback singles, has contributed creative input to the album, Einar Kristiansen Five is handling the mixes, and Linda Eikemo, who also sang on “Madsong,” contributes backing vocals. About Echo Image Echo Image is a Norwegian synthpop band from Fredrikstad, built around Pål-Magnus Rybom. Rybom and Jon-Ivar Berg began experimenting with electronic music in the summer of 1997 and recorded a demo; after Berg left to focus on his own project, Fredrik Hansen and Trine Bilet joined and the band took shape. Echo Image recorded the “Walkout” EP in December 1998 for the local label Kvarts Musikk, then signed to the US synthpop label A Different Drum in 2000, with the German label Bloodline handling European releases; Lars Kristian Holt joined as live guitarist around the same time. The single “Need to Be Proud” was mixed by Apoptygma Berzerk’s Stephan Groth, and the album “Compuphonic” followed in 2001, reaching number 28 on the CMJ RPM chart in the United States. After signing to Hard:Drive for the “Endless Day” single in 2002, Echo Image joined Apoptygma Berzerk on the European “Harmonizer” tour before splitting up later that year. The band reunited in 2016 for the vinyl-only compilation “Compulation” on HolmByKarlsen Rekords, gathering songs from Echo Image’s four earlier releases along with one previously unreleased track. In 2020, Echo Image signed to Pitch Black Drive, the label run by Apoptygma Berzerk’s Stephan Groth, and re-released its back catalogue digitally. The comeback single “Walk My Mind” arrived in March 2021, followed by “Mono No Aware” in 2022 and “Of Truth” in 2023. Rybom, now joined by Linda Eikemo, released the single “Madsong” in February 2024, co-produced by Groth and mixed by Einar Kristiansen Five. In 2025, Rybom lent vocals to German act Elektrostaub’s “Falling” EP on Alfa Matrix. Echo Image’s own next release, the album “My Shadow, My Echo and Me,” is now entering its last stretch after nearly two decades in the making.
items._genre: synthpop / darkwave / electronic
items._cn_summary: Echo Image是一支来自挪威腓特烈斯塔的合成器流行乐队，由Pål-Magnus Rybom主持，1997年组建，2002年解散后于近年回归。新专辑《My Shadow, My Echo and Me》耗时近二十年制作，目前已进入混音与母带处理阶段。专辑标题中的三个词对应Rybom个人经历的不同阶段：阴影代表仍萦绕心头的往事，回声代表支撑他度过低谷的音乐，自我代表穿越风雨后的当下状态。制作团队包括Apoptygma Berzerk成员Stephan Groth担纲创意顾问、Einar Kristiansen Five负责混音、Linda Eikemo参与和声。该作延续了乐队自2021年以来的回归路线，是北欧电子场景中一支相对成熟的合成器流行项目，但整体风格偏主流合成器流行范畴，与实验性或前卫电子路线有一定距离。

Usual Suspects by Jah Wobble & The Invaders Of The Heart “The Usual Suspec
items.body: Jah Wobble & The Invaders Of The Heart reissue the 2xCD collection “The Usual Suspects” on Dimple Discs on November 13, 2026. Originally released in 2017, the 23-track set has been unavailable for years and now changes hands at collectors’ prices; the digital edition is already available on Bandcamp, with the physical 2xCD prepared for that November date to coincide with a UK and Belgium tour. Usual Suspects by Jah Wobble & The Invaders Of The Heart “The Usual Suspects” gathers new recordings of Wobble’s solo material alongside songs from Invaders Of The Heart and his former band Public Image Ltd (PiL), drawn from a catalogue spanning almost forty years at the time of recording. The album was recorded at The Smokehouse studios in East London and opens with a version of PiL’s debut single “Public Image”, reworked from the band’s 1978 debut album. The tracklist also folds in cover versions of two film themes, “Midnight Cowboy” and “Get Carter”, plus Dawn Penn’s “You Don’t Love Me (No, No, No)” featuring vocalist Aurora Dawn, and a new take on “Visions Of You”, which originally featured Sinéad O’Connor on Invaders Of The Heart’s Mercury Prize-nominated 1992 album “Rising Above Bedlam”. The set closes with live recordings of “Liquidator” and “Poptones”, the latter drawn from PiL’s “Metal Box”. Recording personnel on “The Usual Suspects” comprised Jah Wobble on bass, vocals and percussion, Marc Layton-Bennett on drums, percussion and backing vocals, Martin Chung on guitars, George King on keyboards and backing vocals, Steve Rigby on programming and backing vocals, Sean Corby on trumpet and flugelhorn, Aurora Dawn on vocals, and Holly Macve on vocals. Of the band behind the album, Wobble said: “This band has been a delight to play with. Similar to my first early ’80s version of the Invaders, they can all really play, plus all genre bases […] are covered. It’s a big deal to me, because it’s like a 35 year old dream has finally been realised. This is how I heard The Invaders of the Heart sound all those years ago. A classy fusion of genres. Groovy, dubby but always changing and developing. Never standing still.” Tour dates for Jah Wobble & The Invaders Of The Heart The reissue follows a UK tour and comes ahead of Belgian dates in November. Confirmed shows: October 3 – Stourbridge, Katie Fitzgerald’s (UK) October 16 – Todmorden, Unitarian Church (UK) October 21 – Frome, The Tunnels (UK) October 22 – Bristol, The Fleece (UK) October 23 – Reading, Face Bar (UK) November 7 – London, Bush Hall (UK) November 25 – Hasselt, Club AFF (Belgium) November 26 – Bruges, Cactus Muziekcentrum (Belgium) November 27 – Oudenaarde, Harmonie Oudenaarde (Belgium) Tickets are available via Songkick. About Jah Wobble & The Invaders Of The Heart Jah Wobble, born John Wardle, is a bass guitarist and vocalist from East London who was the original bassist in Public Image Ltd alongside John Lydon from the band’s 1978 formation, co-writing and playing on the 1979 album “Metal Box” before leaving in late 1980. He formed Jah Wobble’s Invaders Of The Heart in 1982; that same period brought studio work alongside Can’s Holger Czukay and Jaki Liebezeit, U2 guitarist The Edge, and producer François Kevorkian. Invaders Of The Heart’s commercial peak came with 1991’s “Rising Above Bedlam”, nominated for the Mercury Prize, which included the UK top-40 single “Visions Of You” featuring Sinéad O’Connor. Wobble has since worked with artists including Ginger Baker, Björk, Brian Eno, Baaba Maal, Massive Attack, Sinéad O’Connor, Pharoah Sanders and his wife Zi Lan Liao on guzheng and harp. He reunited with former PiL guitarist Keith Levene in 2012 for the “Metal Box in Dub” shows and the album “Yin & Yang”. Jah Wobble & The Invaders Of The Heart recorded “The Usual Suspects” at The Smokehouse studios in East London, releasing it in 2017 following a six-month UK tour, as covered by Side-Line at the time. More recently, Wobble released the albums “Dub, Vol 1” (2025) and “Automated Paradise” (2026, with former Siouxsie & The Banshees guitarist Jon Klein) on Dimple Discs, and “Mystic Liverpool: The Beatles Psychedelic Songbook” with his sons, who record as Tian Qiyi, released by Cherry Red in August 2026. His autobiography, “Memoirs of a Geezer: Music, Life, Mayhem”, was published by Serpent’s Tail in 2009 and reissued in expanded form as “Dark Luminosity” by Faber & Faber in 2024. Dimple Discs now reissues “The Usual Suspects” as a 2xCD on November 13, 2026, timed to Jah Wobble & The Invaders Of The Heart’s UK and Belgium tour dates.
items._genre: post-punk / dub / world fusion / experimental rock
items._cn_summary: Jah Wobble与The Invaders Of The Heart的2CD合辑《The Usual Suspects》由Dimple Discs于2026年11月再版发行。原版于2017年录制于伦敦东区Smokehouse录音室，收录23首作品，横跨近四十年创作生涯的回顾性合集，开篇为PiL 1978年首张专辑中《Public Image》的重新演绎版本。曲目涵盖PiL时期代表作品、Invaders Of The Heart的多文化融合创作、两首电影主题曲翻唱，以及与Aurora Dawn、Holly Macve等客座歌手的合作。Wobble以贝斯为核心，融合dub、世界音乐与爵士元素，配合铜管与电子编程，构建出多层次的声音景观。再版配合英国与比利时巡演同步推出。整体属于跨界融合范畴，但更偏向回顾性再版而非全新创作。

items.body: Clan of Xymox, the Dutch darkwave and gothic rock project led by Ronny Moorings, released “Notes From The Underground” on 21 September 2001 through Pandaimonium Records in Europe. The album turns 25 this year. Metropolis Records issued it in North America nine days later, on 30 September 2001. Moorings wrote, recorded and mixed all twelve tracks, and produced the record with Mojca Zugna. It was the third studio album of the reformed Clan of Xymox era, after “Hidden Faces” from 1997 and “Creatures” from 1999. Three of its songs were already in circulation by the time it appeared. The “Liberty” CD single, issued by Pandaimonium on 20 October 2000 alongside the band’s double live album, carried “Liberty” together with “Number One” and “At Your Mercy”. Clan of Xymox’s ‘Notes From The Underground’ tracklist and credits The CD runs twelve tracks: “Innocent”, “I Want You Now”, “Internal Darkness”, “At Your Mercy”, “Anguish”, “Number One”, “Into Her Web”, “The Bitter Sweet”, “Liberty”, “Something Wrong”, “Mysterium” and “The Same Dream”. Dierk Budde mastered the album and Mojca Zugna made the sleeve artwork. The band’s official biography states the record reached number 2 on the German DAC chart and topped the US Musicfolio poll for 2001. The same page quotes a Side-Line review of the album as reading “This album is to be seen as a milestone in the band’s discography towards which their previous efforts all converge, or emerge from.” Pandaimonium returned to the material in May 2002 with “Remixes From The Underground”, a two-disc set that reworked every song on the album. Its contributors included Front 242, Assemblage 23, In Strict Confidence, Iris, Angels & Agony and Beborn Beton, and the limited edition added the band’s first video disc. Notes from the Underground by Clan Of Xymox About Clan of Xymox Ronny Moorings formed the band in 1981 in Nijmegen, the Netherlands. Its first release, the mini-album “Subsequent Pleasures”, appeared in 1983 in a run of 500 copies recorded on a four-track home setup. Demo material sent with it led to a deal with 4AD, and the self-titled album followed in 1985, cut at Palladium Studios in Edinburgh and co-produced with label head Ivo Watts-Russell. “Medusa” came next on the same label, and the band contributed “Muscoviet Musquito” to the 4AD compilation “Lonely Is An Eyesore” in 1987. The group parted with 4AD in October 1988, signed to Wing, a PolyGram subsidiary, and shortened its name to Xymox. “Twist of Shadows” arrived in 1989 with the singles “Obsession”, “Imagination” and “Blind Hearts”; the band’s official biography puts its sales above 300,000 copies. “Phoenix” followed in 1991 and closed the Wing chapter when PolyGram wound the label down. “Metamorphosis” and “Headclouds” then came out on the UK independent Zok Records. Moorings also wrote music for two CD-ROM games in the same period, “Total Mayhem” in 1996 and “Revenant” a year later. In 1997 Moorings ended the Xymox era, restarted the band as Clan of Xymox and signed to Tess Records. “Hidden Faces” appeared that year, produced by Dave M. Allen and John A. Rivers. “Creatures” followed in 1999, mixed by Rivers and Moorings, and moved the band to Metropolis Records in North America and Pandaimonium Records in Europe, the pairing that would also handle “Notes From The Underground”. The double live album “LIVE”, drawn from the band’s South and Central American shows, came out in October 2000. “Farewell” arrived in 2003, and “The Best Of Clan Of Xymox”, with its running order chosen by a fan poll, in September 2004. The “Weak In My Knees” EP opened 2006 ahead of the album “Breaking Point”. In early 2009 the band moved to Trisol Records in Europe while staying with Metropolis in the United States, and “In Love We Trust” came out on 18 August 2009, covered in Clan of Xymox’s ‘In Love We Trust’ turns 17 on 18 August. The thirteenth studio album “Darkest Hour” followed on 20 May 2011, the covers set “Kindred Spirits” in October 2012 and “Matters Of Mind, Body And Soul” on 14 February 2014. “Days Of Black” arrived on 7 April 2017, reported in Clan Of Xymox return with new album: ‘Days Of Black’. “Spider On The Wall” followed in 2020, announced in New Clan Of Xymox album ‘Spider On The Wall’ and video for ‘All I Ever Know’, and Moorings talked through his writing that September in Interview with Clan Of Xymox: ‘For Me A Lot Of These Memories Are Finished Stories Without A Soundtrack’. “Limbo”, written during the pandemic lockdowns, arrived in July 2021 and was previewed in Clan Of Xymox returns with all new album ‘Limbo’ in July. The eighteenth album “Exodus” followed in June 2024, reported in Clan Of Xymox announce new album for June: ‘Exodus’, with the “Blood of Christ” EP later that year and a 3CD edition of “Exodus” in February 2025. Moorings looked back across the full run in Ronny Moorings (Clan Of Xymox), an exclusive retrospective interview. Moorings has been the only constant member and still writes, records and produces the band’s music. The live line-up is Moorings on vocals, guitar and melodica, Mojca Zugna on bass, Mario Usai on guitar and bass, and Sean Winzer on keyboards, synth drums and backing vocals. Twenty-five years on, “Notes From The Underground” sits between “Creatures” and “Farewell” in that sequence.

items.body: Bristol project Allflaws released the album The Age Of Nefarious on September 21, 2026, through UK independent label Derelict State Records. The album runs 14 tracks over one hour and one minute, and is available to buy on iTunes and Amazon. Allflaws is the work of Gabriel Curran, who mixes industrial hip hop, trip hop, breakbeat, electronica and dark electronic music on “The Age Of Nefarious”. The album keeps heavy beats, distorted textures and atmospheric production under raw rap vocals, its atmosphere stays tied to Bristol trip hop, but the record leans harder into industrial hip hop’s heavier low end and lets experimental electronica break the production into fractured, glitching textures. Derelict State Records describes the album’s lyrics as exploring control, conformity, digital identity, cultures of violence, low-trust societies, and human resilience. Allflaws’ ‘The Age Of Nefarious’ pushes past the Bristol trip hop sound Derelict State Records, the independent UK label operating out of Bristol and London, works across trip hop, electronica, dub, breakbeat and the darker end of industrial music, including industrial hip hop, industrial electro and EBM. “The Age Of Nefarious” is distributed by Catapult, the same distributor behind Allflaws’ catalog since its earliest releases. An album trailer for “The Age Of Nefarious” is also online on YouTube. Side-Line previously covered Allflaws’ recent standalone singles, including “Vanity Matrix” in 2025, “Chimera” in 2024, and “Antifragile” in 2023. About Allflaws Allflaws was established in Bristol in 2004 by Gabriel Curran, who remains its only official member, writing, producing and performing every release. Curran’s vocal style combines rapping and singing with dark, poetic lyrics, and the project has built its sound around industrial, trip hop and breakbeat elements since its start. Allflaws signed to Catapult and Derelict State Records and released the album “These Walls Are Lies” in 2007, followed by the EPs “Ghost Of The System” and “Replicant Breed” and the album “Black Box Here After” in 2009. The singles “Escaping Sanity” (2010), “Amrak” (2011) and “Interfearence” (2011) preceded the “R Complex” EP and the single “Manufactured Violence” in 2012, and the album “Versus The Soul” in 2013. The album “Apparitions” followed in 2016, then “Mysterium” in 2019 and “Arcana” in 2021. Allflaws released the EP “Ghostrumentals” and the single “Becoming” in 2022, and the single “Antifragile” in 2024. “The Age Of Nefarious”, released September 21, 2026 on Derelict State Records, is Allflaws’ latest full-length, continuing the project’s industrial hip hop and trip hop direction two decades into Curran’s run with Allflaws.
